messages:
lina_support: Hey team — customer reported intermittent 401s, appears only when their key is provisioned via our secrets pipeline and referenced from a URL. Error text: `invalid_api_key`. They pasted a repro curl in the ticket.
sam_eng: Paste the curl here? suspect header formatting.
lina_support: Repro from customer (sanitized):\n\ncurl -v \n  -H "Authorization: Api-Key abc123%25def456ghi789" \n  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \n  -d '{"input":"hello"}' \n  https://api.redwood.inference/v1/generate

They say it works if they manually copy the key from the console, but fails when their infra pulls it from a URL e.g. `https://secrets.company/some/path`.
alex_se: Hmm `%25` is the encoded form of `%`. Looks like the key in their secret store is URL-encoded, then their agent is sending the encoded string literally. Gateway treats that as a different key -> 401. Did they double-encode somewhere?
sam_eng: Can you grep the logs for that exact header value? Lina, do you have proxy logs or request_id from customer?
lina_support: Got their request-id: req_0b3f92. Pasted relevant gateway log (obfuscated):\n\n[2026-11-21T18:02:01Z] req=req_0b3f92 src=10.2.5.8 method=POST path=/v1/generate hdr.Authorization=Api-Key abc123%25def456ghi789 status=401 reason=invalid_api_key\n\nSo the header arriving has `%25` in it.
sam_eng: That points to client-side encoding. Two common patterns: 1) secret value stored URL-encoded in their secret manager, still needs decode before use; 2) their agent runs `encodeURIComponent()` on the key before attaching it to header.
alex_se: Ask them for the secret value raw from the vault. Also ask for stack sample where they read secret. Typical Node pattern: `const key = encodeURIComponent(process.env.API_KEY)` — that would double-encode if the secret already has encoded chars.
lina_support: Customer pasted snippet from their infra: `const key = encodeURIComponent(await secrets.get("/prod/apikey"))` then `headers["Authorization"] = \`Api-Key ${key}\``. They said they added `encodeURIComponent` because of earlier issues with spaces when keys were accidentally copied with spaces.
sam_eng: OK that's the repro. Fix is to stop URL-encoding on attach, or decode when reading. Two suggested fixes: 1) change to `const key = decodeURIComponent(await secrets.get("/prod/apikey"))` if vault stored an encoded value; 2) or remove encode step `const key = (await secrets.get("/prod/apikey")).trim()` if vault stores raw.
alex_se: Also note: If they pass the key via URL or query param somewhere before the header, some HTTP clients may auto-encode. But header encoding is literal — the gateway matches exact bytes. We should document this in our support KB.
lina_support: I told customer to try this quick check: run a local curl with the header value they have from the vault. If curl with that value returns 401 but curl with the console copy works, it's the key encoding. Customer ran a quick test and replied: `confirmed - curl with percent-encoded token 401, unencoded works`.
sam_eng: Good. For mitigation, advise them to rotate the key after fixing pipeline to avoid accidental leakage. Also add to KB: look for `%25`, `+`, `%20`, and other percent encodings in header values when debugging 401s.
deploy-bot: :information_source: Incident note created: INC-20261121-42 — root cause: percent-encoded API key supplied by client agent leading to token mismatch. Status: advisory. Link: https://internal.redwood/incident/INC-20261121-42
alex_se: I pushed a short reply template to the ticket with step-by-step: how to check raw secret, example node/python snippets to decode, and rotate keys. Lina, can you send to customer and close if they're good?
lina_support: Sent the template and the customer confirmed fixed after removing `encodeURIComponent` and rotating the key. They also asked if Redwood can detect and warn when token contains `%25` — is that feasible?
sam_eng: We could add a heuristic on the auth layer to log and optionally warn if the incoming Api-Key contains `%25` or other common encoded sequences. Low-risk to log, medium-risk to auto-decode (don't do auto-decode for security reasons). File a small engineering ticket.
alex_se: Created ticket ENG-2489 in backlog with the suggested heuristic and KB link.
lina_support: Closing thread. Thanks everyone :thumbsup:
